children.name: Matrix
children.doc:
An affine 2D 2x3 matrix.

Matrix properties are as follows:
```
[a, c, x]
[b, d, y]
```

children.name: new
children.doc: Create a new identity Matrix.

children.name: identity
children.doc:
Sets the matrix values to ones that would perform no transformation.
```
[1, 0, 0]
[0, 1, 0]
```

children.name: initTranslate
children.doc:
Sets the matrix values to ones that would only move the transformed positions by given `x` and `y`.
```
[1, 0, x]
[0, 1, y]
```

children.name: initScale
children.doc:
Sets the matrix values to ones that would only scale the transformed positions by given `sx` and `sy`.
```
[sx, 0, 0]
[0, sy, 0]
```

children.name: initRotate
children.doc:
Sets the matrix values to ones that would only rotate the transformed position by given `angle`.
```
[cos(angle), -sin(angle), 0]
[sin(angle),  cos(angle), 0]
```

children.name: initSkew
children.doc:
Sets the matrix values to ones that would only skew the transformed position by given `sx` and `sy`.
```
[1, tan(sx), 0]
[tan(sy), 1, 0]
```

children.name: invert
children.doc:
Inverts the matrix to perform the opposite transformation. Can be used to undo the previously applied transformation.
@see `Matrix.inverse`

children.name: getDeterminant
children.doc: Returns the determinant of the Matrix `a`, `b`, `c` and `d` values.

children.name: inverse
children.doc: Sets this Matrix value to be the inverse of the given Matrix `m`.

children.doc: Returns a new Point that is a result of transforming Point `pt` by this Matrix.

children.doc: Applies translation transform to Matrix by given `x` and `y`.

children.name: translateX
children.doc: Applies translation transform on X-axis to Matrix by given `x`. Equivalent of `matrix.x += x`.

children.name: translateY
children.doc: Applies translation transform on Y-axis to Matrix by given `y`. Equivalent of `matrix.y += y`.

children.name: prependTranslate
children.doc:
Transforms given `x` and `y` with current Matrix values (excluding translation) and
applies translation transform to Matrix by resulting `x` and `y`.

children.name: prependTranslateX
children.doc:
Transforms given `x` with current Matrix values (excluding translation) and
applies translation transform on X-axis to Matrix by resulting `x` and `y`.
Equivalent of `matrix.x += matrix.a * x`.

children.name: prependTranslateY
children.doc:
Transforms given `y` with current Matrix values (excluding translation) and
applies translation transform on Y-axis to Matrix by resulting `y`.
Equivalent of `matrix.y += matrix.d * y`.

children.name: multiply
children.doc:
Concatenates Matrix `a` and `b` and stores the result in this Matrix.
Matrix can be the target of of it's own `multiply`.
Keep in mind that order of matrixes matter in concatenation.

Applies a color correction filter based on the provided matrix.

Matrix values are as following:

Filter
children.doc:
The base filter class, you can extend it in order to define your own filters, although ShaderFilter will be the most straightforward way to define simple custom filter.

Keep in mind that filters use internal Object resolution to render its content, hence scaling of the filtered object would not increase the rendering resolution.
For example, 20x20px `Bitmap` with `scale = 2` will render onto 20x20 filter texture if filter is attached to it directly,
but if filter is attached to the parent of that bitmap, filter will render 40x40 texture.
Another thing to be aware of, is that `Scene.scaleMode` does not affect filter resolution either,
and upscaling contents with `scaleMode` would not upscale the resolution of filtered content.

Filters limit their render area dictated by bound object boundaries, `Filter.autoBounds` and `Filter.boundsExtend` variables and `Filter.getBounds` method.
See their respective docs for details.

For optimization purposes, rendering boundaries are clipped by scene viewport and nothing will be rendered offscreen.

children.name: Anim
children.doc:
Displays an animated sequence of bitmap Tiles on the screen.

Anim does not provide animation sequence management and it's up to user on how to implement it.
Another limitation is framerate. Anim runs at a fixed framerate dictated by `Anim.speed`.
Switching animations can be done through `Anim.play` method.

Note that animation playback happens regardless of Anim visibility and only can be paused by `Anim.pause` flag.
Anim should be added to an active `h2d.Scene` in order to function.

children.name: frames
children.doc:
The current animation, as a list of tile frames to display.
If the frames are empty or if a tile is frames is null, a pink 5x5 bitmap will be displayed instead.

children.name: currentFrame
children.doc:
The current frame the animation is currently playing. Always in `[0,frames.length]` range.
Use `Std.int(anim.currentFrame)` in order to obtain current frame index.
Fractional value represents the progress of current frame and increases according to `Anim.speed` value.

Setting frame to a negative value will wrap it around from the end of the animation. Setting negative value smaller than `-frames.length` lead to undefined behavior.
Setting frame to a value greater than `frames.length` would cause to wrap around.

children.name: speed
children.doc:
The speed (in frames per second) at which the animation is playing.

Settings speed to a negative value is not supported and leads to undefined behavior.

children.name: pause
children.doc: Setting pause will suspend the animation, preventing automatic accumulation of `Anim.currentFrame` over time.

children.name: loop
children.doc: Disabling loop will stop the animation at the last frame.

children.name: fading
children.doc:
When enabled, fading will draw two consecutive frames with alpha transition between
them instead of directly switching from one to another when it reaches the next frame.
This can be used to have smoother animation on some effects.

If `loop` is disabled, callback is sent only once when the animation reaches `currentFrame == frames.length`.
During the call, `currentFrame` is always equals to `frames.length`.

By default, camera does not clip out the contents that are outside camera bounding box, which can be enabled through `Camera.clipViewport`.

Due to Heaps event handling structure, only one Camera instance can handle the mouse/touch input, and can be set through `h2d.Scene.interactiveCamera` variable.
Note that during even handing, interactive camera does not check if the Camera itself is visible nor the layers filters as well as `clipViewport` is not applied.

children.name: Horizontal
children.doc:
Children are aligned horizontally from left to right (or right to left when `Flow.reverse` is enabled).

If `Flow.multiline` is enabled - children can overflow to the next row if there is not enough space available within the Flow size constraints.

`Flow.lineHeight` can be used to set a fixed row height when `Flow.overflow` is set to `Limit` or `Hidden`.
Objects with height that exceed the limitation will be aligned according to `Flow.verticalAlign` value vertically with `null` being treated as `Bottom`.

children.name: Vertical
children.doc:
Children are aligned vertically from top to bottom (or bottom to top when `Flow.reverse` is enabled).

If `Flow.multiline` is enabled - children can overflow to the next column if there is not enough space available within the Flow size constraints.

`Flow.colWidth` can be used to set a fixed column width when `Flow.overflow` is set to `Limit` or `Hidden`.
Objects with height that exceed the limitation will be aligned according to `Flow.horizontalAlign` value horizontally with `null` being treated as `Left`.

children.name: Limit

Children larger than max size will draw outside of the Flow bounds or overflow if `Flow.multiline` is enabled.

children.name: Hidden
children.doc:
Limits the bounds reported by the flow using `Flow.maxWidth` or `Flow.maxHeight`, if set.

Compared to `Limit` - Flow will mask out the content that is outside of Flow bounds.

children.name: Scroll
children.doc: Similar to `Hidden` but allows to scroll using `Flow.scroll*` properties for control.

as it will also capture all other input events, including keyboard events.

Starting event capture through `Interactive.startCapture` will convert `Event.relX` and `relY` to local coordinates
of the Interactive and will restore them after invoking `callb`.
In order to receive coordinates in scene coordinate space use `Scene.startCapture`.

children.doc:
Sent when Interactive is unpressed under multiple circumstances.
Always sent if user releases mouse while it is inside Interactive hitbox area.
			This happens regardless if that Interactive was pressed prior or not,
			and due to that it's not guaranteed that `Interactive.onPush` would precede this event.
			`Event.kind` is set to `ERelease` during this event.
Sent before `Interactive.onReleaseOutside` if this Interactive was pressed, but released outside its hitbox area.
			`Event.kind` is set to `EReleaseOutside` during this event.

		See `Interactive.onClick` and `Interactive.onReleaseOutside` methods for separate events that trigger only when user interacts with this particular Interactive.

Cancelling the `Event` will prevent interactive from becoming overed,

children.name: Object
children.doc:
A base 2D class that all scene tree elements inherit from.

Serves as a virtual container that does not display anything but can contain other objects
so the various transforms are inherited to its children.

Private events `Object.onAdd`, `Object.onRemove` and `Object.onHierarchyMoved` can be used
to capture when Object is added/removed from the currently active scene as well as being moved withing the object tree.

Object exposes a number of properties to control position, scale and rotation of the Object relative to its parent,
but they are used indirectly during rendering. Instead, they are being used to calculate the absolute matrix transform
relative to the Scene. As optimization, it's not recalculated as soon as properties are modified and delayed until
`Object.sync`. Absolute object position can be accessed through private variables `Object.matA`, `Object.matB`,
`Object.matC`, `Object.matD`, `Object.absX` and `Object.absY`.
But it should be noted that in order to ensure up-to-date values, it's advised to call `Object.syncPos` before accessing them.

When set, `Object.alpha` value affects both filter and object transparency (use `Drawable.color.a` to set transparency only for the object).

If there is no `Object.filter` active, only applies to the current object (not inherited by children).

children.name: rebuildOnChange

Note that some parameters take immediate effect on the existing particles, and some would force rebuild regardless of this setting.

Parameters that take immediate effect:
`speedIncr`, `gravity`, `gravityAngle`, `fadeIn`, `fadeOut`, `fadePower`, `rotAuto`, `rotInit`, `incrX`, `incrY`, `emitLoop` and `blendMode`

Parameters that will always force rebuild:
`enable`, `sortMode`, `isRelative`, `texture`, `frameCount`, `frameDivisionX`, `frameDivisionY` and `nparts`

Parameters that newer cause rebuild:
`blendMode`, `colorGradient` and `animationRepeat`

A 2D particle system with wide range of customizability.

The Particles instance can contain multiple `ParticleGroup` instances - each of which works independently from one another.

A simple 9-slice bitmap renderer.

Otherwise calculates center from 0 to the longest line width.

See Text sample for showcase.

A static Tile batch renderer.

entire group have to be cleared with `TileGroup.clear` and repopulated from ground up.

and due to that it's recommended to minimize the amount of used textures per TileGroup instance,
ideally limiting to only one texture.

ZGroup
children.doc:
An advanced double-pass rendering class that utilizes a z-culling on an opaque objects.

	For optimization to work properly, all opaque objects should have `Object.blendMode` set to `None`.

	Rendering is done in two passes:
An opaque pass only renders objects with `blendeMode = None`, with `RenderContext.front2back` and `RenderContext.killAlpha` enabled.
Transparent pass renders the rest of the objects (which are not marked as opaque) as usual.

	That allows to perform a z-cull depth test on the objects and reduce the overall GPU strain.

	Additionally, ZGroup places a limitation on filter usage. They are not drawn in opaque pass, which can lead to undefined behavior.

children.name: clear
children.doc: Put all passes into discarded list

children.name: filter
children.doc: Filter current passes, add results to discarded list

children.name: getFiltered
children.doc: Iterate on all discarded elements, if any

children.name: needStaticUpdate
children.doc: Triggers update of static part of shadows (if any).

children.name: BigPrimitive
children.doc:
Vertex buffers are limited to 65K vertexes because of the 16-bits limitation of the index buffers.
BigPrimitive allows you to easily create large buffers by spliting the buffers.

children.name: begin
children.doc:
Call begin() before starting to add vertexes/indexes to the primitive.
The count value is the number of vertexes you will add, it will automatically flush() if it doesn't fit into the current buffer.

children.name: addPoint
children.doc: This is similar to addVertexValue for X Y and Z, but will also update the bounds if you wish to have them calculated.

children.name: flush
children.doc:
Flush the current buffer.
It is required to call begin() after a flush()

children.name: add
children.doc:
Adds a complete object to the primitive, with custom position,scale,rotation.
See addSub for complete documentation.

children.name: addSub
children.doc:
Adds a buffer to the primitive, with custom position,scale,rotation.
The buffer can have more stride than the BigPrimitive, but not less.
It is assumed that the buffer contains [X,Y,Z,NX,NY,NZ,U,V,R,G,B] (depending on his stride) so the different offsets are applied to the corresponding components.
If hasTangent=true, we have [TX,TY,TZ] just after normal.
However if the stride is 5, we assume [X,Y,Z,U,V]
If mat is not null, it overrides dx, dy, dz, rotation, scale

children.name: defaultUnitCylinder
children.doc:
Get a default unit Cylinder with
segs = 16, ray = 0.5, height = 1.0, centered = false
and add UVs to it. If it has not be cached, it is cached and subsequent
calls to this method will return Cylinder from cache.
@param segs Optional number of segments of the cylinder, default 16

children.name: defaultUnitDisc
children.doc:
Get a default unit Disc with
radius = 0.5, segments = 8, thetaStart = 0.0, thetaLength = Math.PI * 2
and add UVs to it. If it has not be cached, it is cached and subsequent
calls to this method will return Disc from cache.

children.name: minVSize
children.doc: Minimum number of elements in vertex buffer

children.name: minISize
children.doc: Minimum number of elements in index index buffer

children.name: setUVCount
children.doc: Add additional Uv sets that are a copy of the base uv set

children.name: Primitive
children.doc:
h3d.prim.Primitive is the base class for all 3D primitives.
You can't create an instance of it and need to use one of its subclasses.

children.name: buffer
children.doc: The primitive vertex buffer, holding its vertexes data.

children.name: indexes
children.doc: The primitive indexes buffer, holding its triangles indices.

children.name: refCount
children.doc:
Current amount of references to this Primitive.
Use `incref` and `decref` methods to affect this value. If it reaches 0, it will be automatically disposed.

children.name: triCount
children.doc: The number of triangles the primitive has.

children.name: vertexCount
children.doc: The number of vertexes the primitive has.

children.name: getCollider
children.doc: Return a local collider for the primitive

children.name: getBounds
children.doc: Return the bounds for the primitive

children.name: incref
children.doc: Increase reference count of the Primitive.

children.name: decref
children.doc:
Decrease reference count of the Primitive.
If recount reaches zero, Primitive is automatically disposed when last referencing mesh is removed from scene.

children.name: alloc
children.doc: Allocate the primitive on GPU. Used for internal usage.

children.name: selectMaterial
children.doc: Select the specified sub material before drawin. Used for internal usage.

children.name: getMaterialIndexes
children.doc: Returns the number and offset of indexes for the specified material

children.name: render
children.doc: Render the primitive. Used for internal usage.

children.name: dispose
children.doc: Dispose the primitive, freeing the GPU memory it uses.

children.name: toString
children.doc: Return the primitive type.

children.name: lodCount
children.doc: Return the LOD count.

children.name: new
children.doc: You have to pass vertices in this order: top left, top right, bottom left, bottom right

children.name: addUVs
children.doc: Warning : This will splice four basic uv value but can provoke aliasing problems.

children.name: additiveLighting
children.doc:
In the additive lighting model (by default), the lights are added after the ambient.
In the new non additive ligthning model, the lights will be modulated against the ambient, so an ambient of 1 will reduce lights intensities to 0.

children.name: range
children.doc: Alias for uniform scale.

children.name: range
children.doc: Alias for uniform scale.

children.name: BatcherFlags
children.doc: Batcher API

children.name: MeshInstance
children.doc: Batcher Implementation

children.name: set
children.doc:
Set the controller parameters.
Distance is ray distance from target.
Theta and Phi are the two spherical angles
Target is the target position

children.name: loadFromCamera
children.doc:
Load current position from current camera position and target.
Call if you want to modify manually the camera.

children.name: initFromScene
children.doc: Initialize to look at the whole scene, based on reported scene bounds.

children.name: toTarget
children.doc:
Stop animation by directly moving to end position.
Call after set() if you don't want to animate the change

children.name: maxDistance
children.doc: If set, clip all instanced behind this distance.

children.name: enableGpuLod
children.doc:
Enable lod selection at each frame on the gpu using a compute shader.
Has effects only if a lod is available in the primitive.

children.name: enableGpuCulling
children.doc: Enable per instance frustum culling on the gpu using a compute shader.

children.name: enableManualDispatch
children.doc: Enable the user to decide when to call dispatch.

children.name: is3D
children.doc: Setting is3D to true will switch from a screen space line (constant size whatever the distance) to a world space line

children.name: preciseShape
children.doc: If several interactive conflicts, the preciseShape (if defined) can be used to distinguish between the two.

children.name: priority
children.doc: In case of conflicting shapes, usually the one in front of the camera is prioritized, unless you set an higher priority.

children.name: cancelEvents
children.doc: Set the default `cancel` mode (see `hxd.Event`), default to false.

children.name: propagateEvents
children.doc: Set the default `propagate` mode (see `hxd.Event`), default to false.

children.name: enableRightButton
children.doc:
When enabled, interacting with secondary mouse buttons (right button/wheel) will cause `onPush`, `onClick`, `onRelease` and `onReleaseOutside` callbacks.
Otherwise those callbacks will only be triggered with primary mouse button (left button).

children.name: allowMultiClick
children.doc: When enabled, allows to receive several onClick events the same frame.

children.name: bestMatch
children.doc: Is it required to find the best hit point in a complex mesh or any hit possible point will be enough (default = false, faster).

children.name: showDebug
children.doc: When set, will display the debug object of the shape (using makeDebugObj)

children.name: isAbsoluteShape
children.doc: Tells if our shapes are in absolute space (for example ObjectCollider) or relative to the interactive transform.

children.name: preventClick
children.doc: This can be called during or after a push event in order to prevent the release from triggering a click.

children.name: onOver
children.doc:
Sent when mouse enters Interactive hitbox area.
`event.propagate` and `event.cancel` are ignored during `onOver`.
Propagation can be set with `onMove` event, as well as cancelling `onMove` will prevent `onOver`.

children.name: onOut
children.doc:
Sent when mouse exits Interactive hitbox area.
	`event.propagate` and `event.cancel` are ignored during `onOut`.

children.name: onPush
children.doc: Sent when Interactive is pressed by user.

children.name: onRelease
children.doc:
Sent on multiple conditions.
A. Always sent if user releases mouse while it is inside Interactive hitbox area.
	This happends regardless if that Interactive was pressed prior or not.
B. Sent before `onReleaseOutside` if this Interactive was pressed, but released outside it's bounds.
For first case `event.kind` will be `ERelease`, for second case - `EReleaseOutside`.
See `onClick` and `onReleaseOutside` functions for separate events that trigger only when user interacts with this particular Interactive.

children.name: onReleaseOutside
children.doc:
Sent when user presses Interactive, moves mouse outside and releases it.
This event fired only on Interactive that user pressed, but released mouse after moving it outside of Interactive hitbox area.

children.name: onClick
children.doc:
Sent when Interactive is clicked by user.
This event fired only on Interactive that user pressed and released when mouse is inside Interactive hitbox area.

children.name: Mesh
children.doc:
h3d.scene.Mesh is the base class for all 3D objects displayed on screen.
Unlike Object base class, all properties of Mesh only apply to the current object and are not inherited by its children.

children.name: primitive
children.doc: The primitive of the mesh: the list of vertexes and indices necessary to display the mesh.

children.name: material
children.doc: The material of the mesh: the properties used to display it (texture, color, shaders, etc.)

children.name: inheritLod
children.doc: When enabled, the lod level is inherited by children objects.

children.name: blendshapeInstance
children.doc: Instance of the blendshape of the mesh: the list of weights for the different shapes

children.name: forcedLod
children.doc: Allow user to force a specific lod index. If set to -1, forced lod will be ignored.

children.name: new
children.doc:
Creates a new mesh with given primitive, material and parent object.
If material is not specified, a new default material is created for the current renderer.

children.name: getMeshMaterials
children.doc: Return all materials for the current object.

children.name: MeshBatch
children.doc:
h3d.scene.MeshBatch allows to draw multiple meshed in a single draw call.
See samples/MeshBatch.hx for an example.

children.name: shadersChanged
children.doc: Set if shader list or shader constants has changed, before calling begin()

children.name: instanceCount
children.doc: The number of instances on this batch

children.name: worldPosition
children.doc: If set, use this position in emitInstance() instead MeshBatch absolute position

children.name: primitiveSubMeshes
children.doc: Tells the mesh batch to draw only a subpart of the primitive.

children.name: cpuIndirectCallBuffers
children.doc:
Use one indirect call buffer per material.
Instances can not be culled for a specific pass yet.

children.name: calcBounds
children.doc: If set, exact bounds will be recalculated during emitInstance (default true)

children.name: curLod
children.doc:
With EnableCpuLod, set the lod of the next emitInstance.
Without EnableCpuLod and not using primitiveSubMeshes, set the lod of the whole batch.

children.name: enableStorageBuffer
children.doc:
Buffer of per instance params such as position is created as a storage buffer
allowing for huge amount of instances.

children.name: enableGpuUpdate
children.doc:
Buffer of per instance params such as position is created with its own format
allowing compute shaders to update those parameters.

children.name: forceGpuUpdate
children.doc:
Force PerInstance to be setup by a compute shader.
Don't support without Storage Buffer to simplify implementation.

children.name: enableSubMesh
children.doc:
Use sub mesh to emit instance.
Don't support multiple materials without Storage Buffer to simplify implementation.

children.name: enablePerInstanceTexture
children.doc: Enable per instance texture if bindless is supported.

children.name: Object
children.doc:
h3d.scene.Object is the base 3D class that all scene tree elements inherit from.
It can be used to create a virtual container that does not display anything but can contain other objects
so the various transforms are inherited to its children.

children.name: parent
children.doc: The parent object in the scene tree.

children.name: numChildren
children.doc: How many immediate children this object has.

children.name: visible
children.doc: Is the object and its children are displayed on screen (default true).

children.name: culled
children.doc: Inform that the object is not to be displayed and his animation doesn't have to be sync. Unlike visible, this doesn't apply to children unless inheritCulled is set to true.

children.name: alwaysSyncAnimation
children.doc: When an object is not visible or culled, its animation does not get synchronized unless you set alwaysSyncAnimation=true

children.name: inheritCulled
children.doc: When enabled, the culled flag and culling collider is inherited by children objects.

children.name: ignoreBounds
children.doc: When enabled, the object bounds are ignored when using getBounds()

children.name: forceBounds
children.doc: When enabled, the object bounds are included even if it's not visible when using getBounds()

children.name: ignoreCollide
children.doc: When enabled, the object is ignored when using getCollider()

children.name: modelRoot
children.doc: Tag the object as a model root

children.name: ignoreParentTransform
children.doc: When enabled, the object will not follow its parent transform

children.name: lightCameraCenter
children.doc:
When selecting the lights to apply to this object, we will use the camera target as reference
instead of the object absolute position. This is useful for very large objects so they can get good lighting.
(this is only relevant in forward rendering)

children.name: fixedPosition
children.doc:
When set, the object and all its children will not sync() unless this root object position has been changed.
This allows to optimize cpu cost of static objects having many children.
When set, changes on position during sync() won't be applied.

children.name: alwaysSync
children.doc:
When unset, the object and all its children will not sync() if this root object or one of its parent is culled or not visible.
This allows to optimize cpu cost of objects having many children.

children.name: drawn
children.doc: When set, the object has been drawn during previous frame. Useful for temporal effects such as temporal antialiasing.

children.name: cullingCollider
children.doc:
When set, collider shape will be used for automatic frustum culling.
If `inheritCulled` is true, collider will be inherited to children unless they have their own collider set.

children.name: cullingColliderInherited
children.doc: Indicates that current cullingCollider is currently inherited from a parent object

children.name: x
children.doc: The x position of the object relative to its parent.

children.name: y
children.doc: The y position of the object relative to its parent.

children.name: z
children.doc: The z position of the object relative to its parent.

children.name: scaleX
children.doc: The amount of scaling along the X axis of this object (default 1.0)

children.name: scaleY
children.doc: The amount of scaling along the Y axis of this object (default 1.0)

children.name: scaleZ
children.doc: The amount of scaling along the Z axis of this object (default 1.0)

children.name: follow
children.doc: Follow a given object or joint as if it was our parent. Ignore defaultTransform when set.

children.name: followPositionOnly
children.doc: When follow is set, only follow the position and ignore both scale and rotation.

children.name: defaultTransform
children.doc:
This is an additional optional transformation that is performed before other local transformations.
It is used by the animation system.

children.name: name
children.doc: The name of the object, can be used to retrieve an object within a tree by using `getObjectByName` (default null)

children.name: new
children.doc: Create a new empty object, and adds it to the parent object if not null.

children.name: playAnimation
children.doc: Create an animation instance bound to the object, set it as currentAnimation and play it.

children.name: switchToAnimation
children.doc: Change the current animation. This animation should be an instance that was previously created by playAnimation.

children.name: stopAnimation
children.doc: Stop the current animation. If recursive is set to true, all children will also stop their animation

children.name: applyAnimationTransform
children.doc:
When an object is loaded, its position scale and rotation will always be set to the default values (0 for position/rotation and 1 for scale).
If it's part of a group/scene or if it's animated, then its position/rotation/scale will be stored into the defaultTransform matrix.
Calling this function will reset the defaultTransform to null and instead initialize x/y/z/rotation/scale properties.
This will not change the actual position of the object but allows you to move the object more freely on your own.
Do not use on an object that is currently being animated, since it will set again defaultTransform and apply twice the transformation.

children.name: getObjectsCount
children.doc: Return the total number of children, recursively.

children.name: getMaterialByName
children.doc: Search for a material recursively by name, return it or null if not found.

children.name: contains
children.doc: Tells if the object is contained into this object children, recursively.

children.name: find
children.doc: Find a single object in the tree by calling `f` on each and returning the first not-null value returned, or null if not found.

children.name: findAll
children.doc: Find several objects in the tree by calling `f` on each and returning all the not-null values returned.

children.name: getMaterials
children.doc: Return all materials in the tree.

children.name: localToGlobal
children.doc: Convert a local position (or [0,0] if pt is null) relative to the object origin into an absolute global position, applying all the inherited transforms.

children.name: globalToLocal
children.doc: Convert an absolute global position into a local position relative to the object origin, applying all the inherited transforms.

children.name: getInvPos
children.doc: Returns the updated inverse position matrix. Please note that this is not a copy and should not be modified.

children.name: public
children.doc:
Return the bounds of this object and all its children, in absolute global coordinates or relative to the
object being used as parameter.

children.name: getMeshes
children.doc: Return all meshes part of this tree

children.name: getMeshByName
children.doc: Search for an mesh recursively by name, return null if not found.

children.name: getObjectByName
children.doc: Search for an object recursively by name, return null if not found.

children.name: clone
children.doc: Make a copy of the object and all its children.

children.name: addChild
children.doc: Add a child object at the end of the children list.

children.name: addChildAt
children.doc: Insert a child object at the specified position of the children list.

children.name: iterVisibleMeshes
children.doc: Iterate on all mesh that are currently visible and not culled in the tree. Call `callb` for each mesh found.

children.name: removeChild
children.doc: Remove the given object from our immediate children list if it's part of it.

children.name: removeChildren
children.doc: Remove all children from our immediate children list

children.name: remove
children.doc:
Same as parent.removeChild(this), but does nothing if parent is null.
In order to capture add/removal from scene, you can override onAdd/onRemove/onParentChanged

children.name: getScene
children.doc: Return the Scene this object is part of, or null if not added to a Scene.

children.name: getAbsPos
children.doc: Returns the updated absolute position matrix. Please note that this is not a copy so it should not be modified.

children.name: getRelPos
children.doc: Returns the position matrix relative to another scene object

children.name: isMesh
children.doc: Tell if the object is a Mesh.

children.name: toMesh
children.doc: If the object is a Mesh, return the corresponding Mesh. If not, throw an exception.

children.name: public
children.doc:
Build and return the global absolute recursive collider for the object.
Returns null if no collider was found or if ignoreCollide was set to true.

children.name: getGlobalCollider
children.doc: Same as getLocalCollider, but returns an absolute collider instead of a local one.

children.name: getLocalCollider
children.doc:
Build and returns the local relative not-recursive collider for the object, or null if this object does not have a collider.
Does not check for ignoreCollide.

children.name: getPosition
children.doc: Return the (x,y,z) position relative to the object parent.

children.name: setPosition
children.doc: Set the position of the object relative to its parent.

children.name: tmpMat
children.doc: Set the position, scale and rotation of the object relative to its parent based on the specified transform matrix.

children.name: getTransform
children.doc: Returns the local position, scale and rotation of the object relative to its parent.

children.name: rotate
children.doc: Rotate around the current rotation axis by the specified angles (in radian).

children.name: setRotation
children.doc: Set the rotation using the specified angles (in radian).

children.name: setRotationAxis
children.doc: Set the rotation using the specified axis and angle of rotation around it (in radian).

children.name: setDirection
children.doc: Set the rotation using the specified look at direction

children.name: getLocalDirection
children.doc: Return the direction in which the object rotation is currently oriented to

children.name: getRotationQuat
children.doc:
Return the quaternion representing the current object rotation.
Dot not modify as it's not a copy.

children.name: setRotationQuat
children.doc:
Set the quaternion representing the current object rotation.
Dot not modify the value afterwards as no copy is made.

children.name: scale
children.doc: Scale uniformly the object by the given factor.

children.name: setScale
children.doc: Set the uniform scale for the object.

children.name: toString
children.doc: Return both class name and object name if any.

children.name: getChildAt
children.doc: Return the `n`th element among our immediate children list, or null if there is no.

children.name: getChildIndex
children.doc: Return the index of the object `o` within our immediate children list, or `-1` if it is not part of our children list.

children.name: iterator
children.doc: Return an iterator over this object immediate children

children.name: addShader
children.doc: Inject a post process shader for the current frame. Shaders are reset after each render.

children.name: Scene
children.doc: h3d.scene.Scene is the root class for a 3D scene. All root objects are added to it before being drawn on screen.

children.name: camera
children.doc: The scene current camera.

children.name: lightSystem
children.doc: The scene light system. Can be customized.

children.name: renderer
children.doc: The scene renderer. Can be customized.

children.name: scenePosition
children.doc: The scene position. Mainly used for subscenes that aren't fullscreen.

children.name: interactiveOffset
children.doc: Adjust the position of the ray used to handle interactives.

children.name: new
children.doc: Create a new scene. A default 3D scene is already available in `hxd.App.s3d`

children.name: addEventListener
children.doc: Add an event listener that will capture all events not caught by an h2d.Interactive

children.name: removeEventListener
children.doc: Remove a previously added event listener, return false it was not part of our event listeners.

children.name: dispose
children.doc: Free the GPU memory for this Scene and its children

children.name: setElapsedTime
children.doc:
Before render() or sync() are called, allow to set how much time has elapsed (in seconds) since the last frame in order to update scene animations.
This is managed automatically by hxd.App

children.name: syncOnly
children.doc: Synchronize the scene without rendering, updating all objects and animations by the given amount of time, in seconds.

children.name: computeStatic
children.doc: Perform a rendering with `RendererContext.computingStatic=true`, allowing the computation of static shadow maps, etc.

children.name: onContextLost
children.doc: Automatically called when the 3D context is lost

children.name: render
children.doc: Render the scene on screen. Internal usage only.

children.name: setOutputTarget
children.doc:
Temporarily overrides the output render target. This is useful for picture-in-picture rendering,
where the output render target has a different size from the window.
`tex` must have a matching depthBuffer attached.
Call `setOutputTarget()` after `render()` has been called.

children.name: TopDown
children.doc: Sort triangles by Z descending

children.name: dispose
children.doc:
Dispose the World instance.
Note: Only chunked world objects will be disposed. Any objects added to World object will be disposed when World is removed from scene or scene is disposed.

children.name: SAO
children.doc:
Screen space ambient occlusion.
Uses "Scalable Ambient Obscurance" [McGuire12]

children.name: Texture2
children.doc: This is similar to [Texture] shader but uses a second UV set.

children.name: Dynamic
children.doc: Indicate that the buffer content will be often modified.

children.name: NoAlloc
children.doc: Used internaly

children.name: UniformBuffer
children.doc: Used for shader input buffer

children.name: ReadWriteBuffer
children.doc: Can be written

children.name: IndexBuffer
children.doc: Used as index buffer

children.name: screenRatio
children.doc: The screenRatio represents the W/H screen ratio.

children.name: fovY
children.doc:
The vertical FieldOfView, in degrees.
Usually cameras are using an horizontal FOV, but the value will change depending on the screen ratio.
For instance a 4:3 screen will have a lower horizontal FOV than a 16:9 one, however the vertical FOV remains constant.
Use setFovX to initialize fovY based on an horizontal FOV and an initial screen ratio.

children.name: orthoBounds
children.doc: Set orthographic bounds.

children.name: up
children.doc:
up is used for the lookAt matrix.
it is not the actual up axis of the camera.
use getUp instead.

children.name: setFovX
children.doc: Set the vertical fov based on a given horizontal fov (in degrees) for a specified screen ratio.

children.name: getFovX
children.doc: Calculate the current horizontal fov (in degrees).

children.name: getInverseViewProj
children.doc: Returns the inverse of the camera matrix view and projection. Cache the result until the next update().

children.name: getInverseProj
children.doc: Returns the inverse of the camera matrix projection. Cache the result until the next update().

children.name: getInverseView
children.doc: Returns the inverse of the camera matrix view only. Cache the result until the next update().

children.name: getForward
children.doc: Returns the forward of the camera. Cache the result until the next update().

children.name: getRight
children.doc: Returns the right of the camera. Cache the result until the next update().

children.name: getUp
children.doc: Returns the up of the camera. Cache the result until the next update().

children.name: setCubeMap
children.doc: Setup camera for cubemap rendering on the given face.

children.name: unproject
children.doc:
Transforms a 2D screen position into the 3D one according to the current camera.
The screenX and screenY values must be in the [-1,1] range.
The camZ value represents the normalized z in the frustum in the [0,1] range.
[unproject] can be used to get the ray from the camera position to a given screen position by using two different camZ values.
For instance the 3D ray between unproject(0,0,0) and unproject(0,0,1) is the center axis of the 3D frustum.

children.name: projectInline
children.doc: Project a 3D point into the 2D screen. Make sure to update() the camera if it's been moved before using that.

children.name: setRenderZone
children.doc:
Sets up a scissored zone to eliminate pixels outside the given range.
Call with no parameters to reset to full viewport.

children.name: getEulerAngles
children.doc: Extracts Euler rotation angles from rotation matrix

children.name: decomposeMatrix
children.doc:
Extract the rotation from `inMatrix` and stores it as a quaternion inside the [m12,m13,m21,m23] component
instead of the rotation being mixed with the scale.

children.name: recomposeMatrix
children.doc: Inverts the operation of `decomposeMatrix`, giving back a normal transformation matrix from a decomposed one

children.name: lookAtXInline
children.doc: Build a rotation Matrix so the X axis will look at the given direction, and the Z axis will be the Up vector ([0,0,1] by default)

children.name: pow
children.doc: Makes a unit quaternion to the power of the value.

children.name: negate
children.doc: Negate the quaternion: this will not change the actual angle, use `conjugate` for that.

children.name: toMatrix
children.doc: Save to a Left-Handed matrix

children.name: weightedBlend
children.doc:
Blends the sourceQuats together with the given weights and store the result in `this`.
ReferenceQuat is the default rotation to use as the base for the blend
(for example the default rotation of a bone in a skeletal mesh)

children.name: VectorImpl
children.doc: A 3 floats vector. Everytime a Vector is returned, it means a copy is created.

children.name: Vector
children.doc: A 3 floats vector. Everytime a Vector is returned, it means a copy is created.

children.name: Vector4Impl
children.doc: A 4 floats vector. Everytime a Vector is returned, it means a copy is created.

children.name: Vector4
children.doc:
A 4 floats vector. Everytime a Vector is returned, it means a copy is created.
For function manipulating the length (length, normalize, dot, scale, etc.), the Vector

children.name: simplify
children.doc:
Mesh simplifier
Reduces the number of triangles in the mesh, attempting to preserve mesh appearance as much as possible
The algorithm tries to preserve mesh topology and can stop short of the target goal based on topology constraints or target error.
If not all attributes from the input mesh are required, it's recommended to reindex the mesh without them prior to simplification.
Returns the number of indices after simplification, with destination containing new index data
The resulting index buffer references vertices from the original vertex buffer.
If the original vertex data isn't required, creating a compact vertex buffer using optimizeVertexFetch is recommended.

indicesOut must contain enough space for the target index buffer, worst case is indexCount elements (*not* targetIndexCount)!
vertices should have float3 position in the first 12 bytes of each vertex
targetError represents the error relative to mesh extents that can be tolerated, e.g. 0.01 = 1% deformation; value range [0..1]
options must be a bitmask composed of meshopt_SimplifyX options; 0 is a safe default
resultErrorOut can be null; when it's not null, it will contain the resulting (relative) error after simplification

children.name: simplifyWithUpdate
children.doc:
Mesh simplifier with position/attribute update
Reduces the number of triangles in the mesh, attempting to preserve mesh appearance as much as possible.
Similar to meshopt_simplifyWithAttributes, but destructively updates positions and attribute values for optimal appearance.
The algorithm tries to preserve mesh topology and can stop short of the target goal based on topology constraints or target error.
If not all attributes from the input mesh are needed, it's recommended to reindex the mesh without them prior to simplification.
Returns the number of indices after simplification, indices are destructively updated with new index data

The updated index buffer references vertices from the original vertex buffer, however the vertex positions and attributes are updated in-place.
Creating a compact vertex buffer using meshopt_optimizeVertexFetch is recommended; if the original vertex data is needed, it should be copied before simplification.
Note that the number of attributes with non-zero weights affects memory requirements and running time. Attributes with zero weights are not updated.

vertexPos should have float3 position in the first 12 bytes of each vertex
vertexAttributes should have attributeCount floats for each vertex
attributeWeights should have attributeCount floats in total; the weights determine relative priority of attributes between each other and wrt position
attributeCount must be <= 32
vertexLock can be null; when it's not null, it should have a value for each vertex composed of meshopt_SimplifyVertex_* flags
targetError represents the error relative to mesh extents that can be tolerated, e.g. 0.01 = 1% deformation (unless absolute error option is used)
options must be a bitmask composed of meshopt_SimplifyX options; 0 is a safe default
resultErrorOut can be null; when it's not null, it will contain the resulting (relative/absolute) error after simplification

children.name: optimizeVertexCache
children.doc:
Vertex transform cache optimizer
Reorders indices to reduce the number of GPU vertex shader invocations
If index buffer contains multiple ranges for multiple draw calls, this functions needs to be called on each range individually.

indicesOut must contain enough space for the resulting index buffer (indexCount elements)

children.name: optimizeOverdraw
children.doc:
Overdraw optimizer
Reorders indices to reduce the number of GPU vertex shader invocations and the pixel overdraw
If index buffer contains multiple ranges for multiple draw calls, this functions needs to be called on each range individually.

indicesOut must contain enough space for the resulting index buffer (indexCount elements)
indicesIn must contain index data that is the result of optimizeVertexCache (*not* the original mesh indices!)
vertices should have float3 position in the first 12 bytes of each vertex
threshold indicates how much the overdraw optimizer can degrade vertex cache efficiency (1.05 = up to 5%) to reduce overdraw more efficiently

children.name: optimizeVertexFetch
children.doc:
Vertex fetch cache optimizer
Reorders vertices and changes indices to reduce the amount of GPU memory fetches during vertex processing
Returns the number of unique vertices, which is the same as input vertex count unless some vertices are unused

verticesOut must contain enough space for the resulting vertex buffer (vertexCount elements)
indices is used both as an input and as an output index buffer

children.name: generateTangents
children.doc:
Computes per-corner tangent vectors; for each corner, computes normalized tangent vector (xyz) and orientation (w, +/-1).
Bitangent can be reconstructed via cross(normal, tangent.xyz) * tangent.w.
To apply tangents to the mesh, either deindex and reindex it with the tangent stream, or copy tangents to existing vertex data while duplicating
vertices with different tangent vectors (e.g. on UV mirror seams).
Input can be indexed or unindexed (indices=NULL); this does not affect the resulting tangents, but indexed inputs are ~30% faster to process.

result must contain enough space for the output tangent data (indexCount*4 elements)
indices can be NULL if the input is unindexed
vertexPos should have float3 position in the first 12 bytes of each vertex
vertexNormals should have unit float3 normal in the first 12 bytes of each vertex
vertexUVs should have float2 texture coordinate in the first 8 bytes of each vertex

children.name: Save
children.doc:
Save provides simple interface to save and load serialized user data.
Data is serialized to String with `haxe.Serializer` and then stored in text form.

children.name: load
readSaveData
children.doc:
Override this method to provide custom save lookup.
		By default it uses `name + ".sav"` for system targets and `localStorage.getItem(name)` on JS.
*Note:** This method is an utility method, to load data use `hxd.Save.load`

children.name: writeSaveData
children.doc:
Override this method to provide custom save storage.
		By default it stores saves in `name + ".sav"` file in current working directory on system targets and `localStorage.setItem(name)` on JS.
*Note:** This method is an utility method, to save data use `hxd.Save.save`

children.name: delete
children.doc:
Deletes save with specified name.
Override this method when using custom save lookup.

children.name: save
children.doc:
Saves `val` under the specified name.
@param checkSum When set, save data is prepended by salted crc checksum for data validation. When save is loaded, `checkSum` flag should be set accordingly.

children.name: Timer
children.doc:
The Timer class acts as a global time measurement that can be accessed from various parts of the engine.
These three values are representation of the same underlying calculus: tmod, dt, fps

children.name: wantedFPS
children.doc:
The FPS on which "tmod" have values are based on.
Can be freely configured if your gameplay runs at a different speed.
Default : 60

children.name: maxDeltaTime
children.doc:
The maximum amount of time between two frames (in seconds).
If the time exceed this amount, Timer will consider these lags are to be ignored.
Default : 0.5

children.name: smoothFactor
children.doc:
The smoothing done between frames. A smoothing of 0 gives "real time" values, higher values will smooth
the results for tmod/dt/fps over frames using the formula   dt = lerp(elapsedTime, dt, smoothFactor)
Default : 0 on HashLink, 0.95 on other platforms

children.name: lastTimeStamp
children.doc: The last timestamp in which update() function was called.

children.name: elapsedTime
children.doc: The amount of time (unsmoothed) that was spent since the last frame.

children.name: frameCount
children.doc: A frame counter, increases on each call to update()

children.name: dt
children.doc: The smoothed elapsed time (in seconds).

children.name: tmod
children.doc:
The smoothed frame modifier, based on wantedFPS. Its value is the same as dt/wantedFPS
Allows to express movements in terms of pixels-per-frame-at-wantedFPS instead of per second.

children.name: update
children.doc: Update the timer calculus on each frame. This is automatically called by hxd.App

children.name: fps
children.doc: The current smoothed FPS.

children.name: skip
children.doc:
After some loading / long processing, call skip() in order to prevent
it from impacting your smoothed values.

children.name: reset
children.doc:
Similar as skip() but also reset dt to default value.
Can be used when starting a new game if you want to discard any previous measurement.
